title: FOXO3A genotype is strongly associated with human longevity.
venue: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
key_point: Candidate-gene nested case-control in long-lived Japanese-American men; FOXO3A homozygous minor vs major OR 2.75 (P=0.00009).

title: Association of FOXO3A variation with human longevity confirmed in German centenarians.
venue: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
key_point: 1,762 German centenarians/nonagenarians vs younger controls; FOXO3A association considerably stronger in centenarians than nonagenarians.

title: Genetic signatures of exceptional longevity in humans.
key_point: New England Centenarian Study GWAS (801 centenarians, median age at death 104); 281-SNP genetic signatures model, clusters of signatures correlate with different lifespans.

title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis of human longevity identifies a novel locus conferring survival beyond 90 years of age.
key_point: >=85 y cases (7,729) vs <65 y controls; rs2149954 (5q33.3) OR 1.10 for survival beyond 90; prospective meta-analysis HR 0.95; minor T allele linked to low midlife blood pressure and lower CV mortality. rs4420638 (APOE) OR 0.72.

title: GWAS of longevity in CHARGE consortium confirms APOE and FOXO3 candidacy.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: CHARGE: >=90 y cases (6,036) vs controls dying 55-80 y; only APOE and FOXO3 replicated; suggestive CADM2, GRIK2.

title: Novel loci and pathways significantly associated with longevity.
key_point: Han Chinese centenarian GWAS; novel genome-wide loci IL6 rs2069837 and ANKRD20A9P rs2440012.

title: Four Genome-Wide Association Studies Identify New Extreme Longevity Variants.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: 2,070 oldest-1% survivors; separates extreme-survival variants from variants enriched in centenarians only by mortality selection at younger ages.

title: Sex Differences in Genetic Associations With Longevity.
key_point: CLHLS sex-specific GWAS: >100 y (564 men, 1,614 women) vs 40-64 y controls.

title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies multiple longevity genes.
key_point: Cases at/above 90th (n=11,262) or 99th (n=3,484) survival percentile vs 25,483 controls at/below 60th percentile. European discovery Table 2: rs429358 (APOE e4) C OR 0.60 (90th) vs 0.52 (99th); rs7412 (e2) T OR 1.28 (90th) vs 1.47 (99th); authors note most variants are stronger at the 99th percentile. CDKN2A/B rs7039467 A OR 1.20 (99th, P=1.1e-7, suggestive).

title: A Genome-Wide Association Study of 2304 Extreme Longevity Cases Identifies Novel Longevity Variants.
key_point: >99th survival percentile, 2,304 cases vs 5,879 controls; CDKN2B-AS1 rs6475609 P=7.13e-8 (near genome-wide).

title: HLA-DRB1*15:01 is associated with a reduced likelihood of longevity in northern European men.
key_point: HLA-DRB1*15:01:01 male-specific lower odds of longevity (OR 0.64, adj P=0.028) in Germans; replicated in UK Biobank, consistent in Danes.

title: Age-stratified genomic analyses reveal population-specific genetic determinants of exceptional longevity in Taiwan.
key_point: Taiwan, thresholds >=85/>=90/>=95 y; PRS AUC gain largest at >=95 (0.913 to 0.956); European/Han loci APOE (rs429358, rs7412) and FOXO3 weak or absent; abstract reports age-dependent genetic architecture.

title: APOE Alleles and Extreme Human Longevity.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: 28,297 participants, 7 studies: e4 reduces odds of extreme longevity and raises death risk that persists beyond ages reached by <1%; e2 raises odds of extreme longevity but gives only a modest reduction in death risk beyond that age.

title: CHRNA5 risk variant predicts delayed smoking cessation and earlier lung cancer diagnosis--a meta-analysis.
key_point: CHRNA5 rs16969968 AA: 4-year delay in quitting and 4-year earlier median lung-cancer diagnosis vs GG (HR 1.08).

title: Polygenic and clinical risk scores and their impact on age at onset and prediction of cardiometabolic diseases and common cancers.
key_point: FinnGen: high PRS gives 4-9 years earlier onset of CHD, T2D, AF, breast and prostate cancer.

title: The impact of age on genetic risk for common diseases.
key_point: UKB, 24 diseases, age-varying proportional hazards: 9 diseases show age-varying genetic RR (incl. hypertension, skin cancer, atherosclerotic heart disease); predominant pattern is greatest RR at early onset, decreasing with age.

title: Case-control association mapping by proxy using family history of disease.
key_point: GWAX: replacing cases by first-degree relatives (proxy) for late-onset/lethal disease; method underlying parental designs.

title: Variants near CHRNA3/5 and APOE have age- and sex-related effects on human lifespan.
key_point: 272,081 parental lifespans (>40 y). APOE e4 HR 1.09 in mothers dying 40-75 vs 1.20 over 75 (0.2 life-years lost before 75, 1.1 after); CHRNA3/5 rs10519203 HR 1.10 vs 1.03 in fathers (0.5 vs 0.1 years). Age contrast P<0.006 in the more-affected sex.

title: Human longevity: 25 genetic loci associated in 389,166 UK biobank participants.
key_point: 389,166 UKB. Attained age: 10 loci. Both parents in top 10% (father >=87, mother >=90) confirmed APOE, CHRNA3, LPA, CDKN2B-AS1 (ATXN2 suggestive P=3.4e-6); MC2R rs28926173 P=2.3e-8 for top-10% but only 6.4e-6 for attained age.

title: Genomics of 1 million parent lifespans implicates novel pathways and common diseases and distinguishes survival chances.
key_point: ~1M parental lifespans. Age-band source data (Fig 5 data 1/2) for 24 variants: APOE e4 log HR over 70 ~3x that at 40-70 (age-moderator P=2.2e-14); CHRNA3/5 (q=0.0048), ABO (q=0.0086), CDKN2B-AS1 (q=0.011) decline after age 60.

title: A Prospective Analysis of Genetic Variants Associated with Human Lifespan.
key_point: AncestryDNA + UKB (>650,000): 15 parental-lifespan loci; GWAS of age itself found only APOE.

title: Human longevity is influenced by many genetic variants: evidence from 75,000 UK Biobank participants.
key_point: 75,244 UKB; CHRNA3 for fathers; offspring of longer-lived parents carry more protective alleles for CAD, SBP, BMI and other risk factors.

title: Bayesian association scan reveals loci associated with human lifespan and linked biomarkers.
key_point: Bayesian scan with priors from 58 disease GWAS; 16 SNPs; all but three depleted of life-shortening alleles in older Biobank participants; RBM6, SULT1A1, CHRNA5.

title: Genome-wide meta-analysis associates HLA-DQA1/DRB1 and LPA and lifestyle factors with human longevity.
key_point: 606,059 parents; new HLA-DQA1/DRB1 and LPA; validates APOE, CHRNA3/5, CDKN2A/B, SH2B3, FOXO3A; MR: +1 BMI unit = -7 months, +1 year education = +11 months.

title: The Longevity-Associated SH2B3 (LNK) Genetic Variant: Selected Aging Phenotypes in 379,758 Subjects.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: SH2B3 rs3184504 C: CHD OR 0.95 but cancer OR 1.03 (trade-off); associated with parental extreme longevity.

title: Limited overlap between genetic effects on disease susceptibility and disease survival.
key_point: Nine diseases, seven biobanks: limited overlap between genetic effects on susceptibility and on disease-specific mortality.

title: Age, gender, and cancer but not neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases strongly modulate systemic effect of the Apolipoprotein E4 allele on lifespan.
key_point: FHS/LLFS: adverse e4 effect limited to women with lifespans of ~70-95 y (RR 1.48); not mediated by CVD, ND or cancer.

title: The impact of APOE genotype on survival: Results of 38,537 participants from six population-based cohorts (E2-CHARGE).
key_point: 38,537 (mean age 65.5), 6 cohorts: e2 carriers HR 0.94, e4 carriers HR 1.17, e4e4 HR 1.52; e4 attenuated to 1.07 after censoring for dementia; results did not differ by age or sex.

title: A genome-wide association study of aging.
key_point: CHARGE 9 cohorts, all-cause mortality and event-free survival; no genome-wide significant SNP.

title: Rare genetic associations with human lifespan in UK Biobank are enriched for oncogenic genes.
key_point: UKB own survival (35,551 deaths); common APOE, ZSCAN23; LoF burden TET2, ATM, BRCA2, CKMT1B, BRCA1, ASXL1 shorten life; signals predominantly cancer-driven.

title: Trans-biobank analysis with 676,000 individuals elucidates the association of polygenic risk scores of complex traits with human lifespan.
key_point: BBJ+UKB+FinnGen (675,898): SBP PRS and BMI PRS associate with shorter lifespan; MR supports BP and obesity as causal.

title: Identification of 12 genetic loci associated with human healthspan.
key_point: UKB 300,447: healthspan = age at first of 7 major diseases or death; disease risks double every ~8 years; 12 loci.

title: Genomic structural equation modelling provides insights into the multivariate genetic architecture of complex traits.
key_point: Genomic SEM method (common-factor GWAS from summary statistics).

title: Multivariate genomic scan implicates novel loci and haem metabolism in human ageing.
key_point: Healthspan + parental lifespan + longevity MANOVA: 10 loci (new FOXO3, SLC4A7, LINC02513, ZW10, FGD6). Age-stratified: APOE e4 effect +32%/decade of parental survival; the other nine loci collectively -24%/decade.

title: Mendelian randomization of genetically independent aging phenotypes identifies LPA and VCAM1 as biological targets for human aging.
key_point: aging-GIP1 = first genetic PC of 6 ageing traits; 27 regions; HTT and MAML3 supported; MR+coloc: apo(a) and VCAM1 detrimental.

title: Multivariate genome-wide analysis of aging-related traits identifies novel loci and new drug targets for healthy aging.
key_point: mvAge genomic SEM (effective n ~1.9M): 52 variants in 38 loci; drug-target MR (metformin targets, ANGPTL4, beta blockers, CCBs).

title: Identifying genetic variants that affect viability in large cohorts.
key_point: Allele-frequency change with age (GERA; UKB parents): genome-wide only APOE e4 and CHRNA3. e4-tag rs6857 risk allele declines monotonically beyond age 70; CHRNA3 rs1051730 A declines linearly over almost all paternal ages; PGS for later puberty linked to longer parental life.

title: Familial excess longevity in Utah genealogies.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: Utah genealogies (78,994): familial excess longevity h2 ~0.15; sibling relative risk 2.30 at the 97th percentile.

title: Longevity defined as top 10% survivors and beyond is transmitted as a quantitative genetic trait.
key_point: UPDB + LINKS (314,819 individuals): longevity transmitted as a quantitative trait up to the top 10% survivors; up to 31% survival advantage with top-10% relatives.

title: Longevity Relatives Count score identifies heritable longevity carriers and suggests case improvement in genetic studies.
key_point: LRC score: longevity transmitted only when >=20% of relatives are long-lived (1,326 five-generation families).

title: Improved selection of participants in genetic longevity studies: family scores revisited.
key_point: Model-based mLRC score improves case selection over LRC.

title: Genome-wide association study (GWAS)-identified disease risk alleles do not compromise human longevity.
venue: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
key_point: Nonagenarian siblings and >85 y singletons carry the same number of GWAS risk alleles for CAD, cancer, T2D as young controls.

title: Genome-Wide Scan Informed by Age-Related Disease Identifies Loci for Exceptional Human Longevity.
key_point: iGWAS: disease-GWAS priors; disease variants depleted in centenarians.

title: Polygenic Risk Score of Longevity Predicts Longer Survival Across an Age Continuum.
venue: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
key_point: 330-variant longevity PRS (cognitively healthy centenarians vs older adults) predicts survival in younger people and partly compensates for APOE e4.

title: Increased genetic protection against Alzheimer's disease in centenarians.
key_point: Non-APOE AD polygenic protective score higher in centenarians and higher still with greater age at death (105-109, >=110).

title: Low genetic risk for coronary artery disease underlies multigenerational longevity and healthy aging.
key_point: Leiden Longevity Study: more long-lived ancestors additively associated with lower CAD PGS; CAD PGS explains up to 20% of delayed CVD in descendants; cholesterol-metabolism PGS predicts mortality in two 90+ cohorts.

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of a Healthy Aging Cohort.
key_point: Wellderly WGS: healthy ageing linked to lower AD and CAD genetic risk, not to fewer rare pathogenic variants.

title: Similar burden of pathogenic coding variants in exceptionally long-lived individuals and individuals without exceptional longevity.
key_point: Ashkenazi centenarians vs offspring vs controls (n=1,879): same burden of ClinVar/HGMD pathogenic variants.

title: Functionally significant insulin-like growth factor I receptor mutations in centenarians.
venue: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
key_point: IGF1R mutations enriched in Ashkenazi centenarians, with high serum IGF-I and reduced IGF1R activity.

title: Human knockouts and phenotypic analysis in a cohort with a high rate of consanguinity.
key_point: PROMIS 10,503 exomes: homozygous pLoF human knockouts; APOC3 knockouts blunted postprandial triglyceride rise.

title: Germline burden of rare damaging variants negatively affects human healthspan and lifespan.
key_point: Burden of rarest PTVs shortens healthspan and lifespan (0.4 and 1.3 years of variability).

title: The burden of rare protein-truncating genetic variants on human lifespan.
key_point: 352,338 exomes: PTV burden in BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, TET2 associated with shorter own/parental lifespan; modest overlap with common-variant GWAS.

title: German longevity study reveals novel rare pro-longevity alleles clustering in mTOR signaling pathway.
key_point: 1,245 German long-lived vs 4,105 controls: rare variants in mTOR-pathway genes (RPS6, FLCN, SIK3), RWDD1 burden; ASXL1/TET2 PTVs reflect clonal haematopoiesis.

title: Rare genetic coding variants associated with human longevity and protection against age-related diseases.
key_point: Ashkenazi centenarian exomes: rare coding variants converge on IIS and AMPK pathways; Wnt-pathway rare variants pro-longevity in APOE4 carriers; pathogenic-variant counts similar to controls.

title: Sequence variations in PCSK9, low LDL, and protection against coronary heart disease.
key_point: ARIC 15-year: PCSK9 nonsense (black, 2.6%) LDL -28%, CHD HR 0.11; R46L-type variant (white, 3.2%) LDL -15%, CHD HR 0.50.

title: Phenotypic Characterization of Genetically Lowered Human Lipoprotein(a) Levels.
key_point: LPA LoF alleles lower CHD; genetically lower Lp(a) also lowers PAD, stroke, heart failure, aortic stenosis.

title: Unique lipoprotein phenotype and genotype associated with exceptional longevity.
key_point: Centenarians and offspring: larger HDL/LDL particle size, more CETP I405V homozygosity.

title: Trade-offs in the effects of the apolipoprotein E polymorphism on risks of diseases of the heart, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders: insights on mechanisms from the Long Life Family Study.
key_point: LLFS: age/sex-specific e4 trade-offs (heart disease, cancer, neurodegeneration); e4 neurological RR 1.98.

title: Antagonistic pleiotropy and mutation accumulation influence human senescence and disease.
key_point: Variants for early-onset diseases under stronger purifying selection; late-onset disease variants show antagonistic-pleiotropy patterns.

title: Genetic loci associated with coronary artery disease harbor evidence of selection and antagonistic pleiotropy.
key_point: CAD loci carry selection signals and antagonistic pleiotropy with reproductive traits.

title: Antagonistic Pleiotropy in Human Disease.
key_point: Review of antagonistic pleiotropy evidence in human disease.

title: Pan-mammalian analysis of molecular constraints underlying extended lifespan.
key_point: Pan-mammalian rates of protein evolution vs lifespan: increased constraint in many longevity-associated pathways.

title: Evidence for the role of selection for reproductively advantageous alleles in human aging.
key_point: UKB 276,406: strong negative genetic correlation of reproductive traits with lifespan; higher reproduction PGS = lower survival to 76.

title: Trade-off in the effect of the APOE gene on the ages at onset of cardiocascular disease and cancer across ages, gender, and human generations.
key_point: FHS: e4 carriers live longer without cancer; e4 effect on CVD onset is age-, sex- and generation-specific (trade-off).

title: Effect of APOE ε4 allele on survival and fertility in an adverse environment.
key_point: Rural Ghana (n=4,311): APOE e4 promotes fertility in a high-pathogen environment; framed as antagonistic pleiotropy.

title: GWAS of epigenetic aging rates in blood reveals a critical role for TERT.
key_point: Epigenetic age acceleration GWAS (9,907): TERT alleles for longer telomeres paradoxically increase IEAA.

title: Genome-wide association studies identify 137 genetic loci for DNA methylation biomarkers of aging.
key_point: 137 loci for DNAm clocks (>40,000); GrimAge PGS associated with parental longevity and adiposity.

title: Effect of longevity genetic variants on the molecular aging rate.
key_point: Centenarian GWAS variants linked to slower change in serum protein ageing markers; CDKN2A/B rs2184061 GDF15 signature.

title: Integrating the environmental and genetic architectures of aging and mortality.
key_point: Exposome vs polygenic risk; proteomic age clock (n=45,441); exposures explain more mortality variation than PRS.

title: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype-associated disease risks: a phenome-wide, registry-based, case-control study utilising the UK Biobank.
key_point: UKB PheWAS of APOE genotypes: 37 outcomes/18 diseases; possible e4-linked protection for some conditions.
